screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of aminophylline in acute ischemic stroke; intervention initiated in the acute phase (within hospitalization), consistent with ≤1-week window.
Double-blind randomized trial of IV aminophylline vs placebo in acute cerebral infarction; acute administration aligns with ≤1-week onset criterion.
Open-label, single-arm dose-escalation safety study with no randomization or control group, despite acute administration.
Physiological/metabolic study across general subjects; not an RCT in acute ischemic stroke versus placebo/control; population and timing not aligned.
Randomized cross-over physiological study in patients recovering from stroke (not within 1 week of onset); not a therapeutic RCT for acute AIS outcomes.
Randomized cross-over physiological CBF study in recovering stroke patients; not within acute (≤1-week) window and not a therapeutic RCT vs control.
Small physiological infusion study without randomization or clear acute ischemic stroke population; no placebo/control.
Animal experiment (cats); not a randomized clinical trial in humans with acute ischemic stroke.
Animal study in anesthetized dogs; not a human RCT in acute ischemic stroke.
Mechanistic/overview with uncontrolled observations; not a randomized, placebo-controlled acute ischemic stroke trial.
